answer: A work-history ledger makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent carries a vine of completed, counterparty-signed tasks, and trust grows only as that vine lengthens. A fresh identity is a bare willow twig — it can observe but cannot take paid work until others vouch for real deliveries. A mirror check compares each claimed history against the ledger, so copied reputations fail instantly. Forging a hundred credible identities means doing a hundred histories of real work, which costs more than the attack gains.
